_meta.purpose: Statutory and customary charges on buying a home, by city, for the home-buying tool. Every rate is a percentage of the higher of agreement value and the state's guideline (circle / ready-reckoner) value; the tool uses the price the user types.

confidence_key.verified: Confirmed from the state registration department or two or more lender pages agreeing on the number and the date.
confidence_key.corroborated: Several secondary sources agree; no primary text retrieved. Check before relying on it for a purchase.
confidence_key.unverified: Sources conflict. The tool shows a warning next to this figure.

_meta.review_note: Stamp duty changes by state budget and notification, usually in April or at any time by government order. Re-check all seven cities every quarter.

stamp_duty.composition: 5% stamp duty + 1% metro cess. Women buying residential property in their sole name pay 1 point less; the earlier 15-year resale restriction on that concession was removed.

registration.note: 1% of value, capped at ₹30,000 (properties above ₹30 lakh pay the cap).

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on the loan agreement / mortgage deed (0.3% of loan, max ₹5 lakh). Some lenders charge 0.2% for a deposit of title deeds.

stamp_duty.composition: 5% stamp duty + 1% metro cess + 1% local body tax (LBT). Women buying residential property in their sole name pay 1 point less.

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on the mortgage deed (0.3% of loan, max ₹5 lakh).

stamp_duty.composition: 6% for a man, 4% for a woman, 5% when a man and a woman buy jointly. Applies on the higher of agreement value and circle rate.

registration.note: 1% of value plus ₹100 pasting fee. No cap.

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on the mortgage / loan agreement; lenders quote about 0.2% of the loan. Varies with the instrument used.

stamp_duty.composition: 2% up to ₹20 lakh, 3% from ₹20 to ₹45 lakh, 5% above ₹45 lakh; plus 10% cess and 2% surcharge levied on the duty itself inside BBMP limits (5% becomes 5.6%). No gender concession.
stamp_duty.conflict: One lender page describes the add-on as a flat 0.5% cess on the duty; most describe 10% cess + 2% surcharge on the duty (0.6 points on a 5% duty). The larger figure is used.

registration.note: Registration fee doubled from 1% to 2% of value from 31 August 2025.

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on deposit of title deeds, 0.1% of loan, max ₹10,000.

stamp_duty.composition: 4% stamp duty + 1.5% transfer duty. No gender concession. With the 0.5% registration fee the statutory total is 6%.

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on the mortgage deed in Telangana, about 0.5% of the loan. Check with the lender.

stamp_duty.composition: 7% of the higher of market and guideline value. No gender concession on stamp duty.

registration.note: 4% of value, the highest of the seven cities: statutory total 11%. Women buying property up to ₹10 lakh pay 3% (not modelled; below the price range this tool is for).

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on deposit of title deeds, 0.1% of loan, capped.

stamp_duty.composition: 6% within Kolkata Municipal Corporation for value up to ₹1 crore, 7% above ₹1 crore (the extra 1% applies to the whole value once it crosses ₹1 crore). No gender concession. The 2% pandemic rebate ended in June 2024.

mortgage_deed_stamp.note: Stamp duty on the mortgage instrument; lenders quote 0.2% to 0.5% of the loan depending on the instrument.

gst.affordable_definition: Carpet area up to 60 sq m in a metro (90 sq m elsewhere) and value up to ₹45 lakh.
gst.note: GST applies only to under-construction property bought from a builder, on the agreement value; none on a completed property with an occupancy certificate or on resale. The 5% / 1% rates are without input tax credit.

brokerage.note: Brokerage on resale is 1% to 2% of the price, sometimes plus GST at 18% on the fee. Nil on most builder sales (the builder pays the channel partner).

legal_and_valuation.note: Lawyer's title search and the lender's valuation and legal fees, typically ₹5,000 to ₹15,000 combined.

loan_processing_fee.note: Most lenders charge 0.25% to 0.5% of the loan, often capped; some run flat-fee or zero-fee offers.

customary.tds_note: If the price is ₹50 lakh or more you must deduct 1% TDS from what you pay the seller and deposit it (Form 26QB). It is part of the price, not an extra cost, but it is a compliance step on the day.
